reasoning: Verified against a vendored duckdb.h (typedef uint64_t idx_t; h:243) and the current ducklib.py. All cited idx_t returns/args ARE idx_t in duckdb.h: duckdb_column_count (h:995), duckdb_row_count (h:1006), duckdb_data_chunk_get_column_count (h:2957), duckdb_data_chunk_get_size (h:2976), and the 'row' arg of duckdb_validity_row_is_valid (h:3171: 'idx_t row'). ducklib.py declares them intp instead of uint64 at exactly the cited lines: L106 duckdb_column_count=intp(intp), L156 duckdb_data_chunk_get_column_count=intp(intp), L157 duckdb_data_chunk_get_size=intp(intp), L226 duckdb_row_count=intp(intp), L234 duckdb_validity_row_is_valid=int8(intp, intp) (2nd arg is the idx_t row). Sibling idx_t returns are correctly uint64 (L78 duckdb_array_type_array_size, L189 duckdb_get_list_size, L217 duckdb_nparams, L228 duckdb_struct_type_child_count), confirming the inconsistency is real and internal to this file. duckdb_vector_get_validity genuinely returns 'uint64_t *' (h:3043, a pointer) but ducklib.py L237 declares it uint64 (scalar) rather than intp, breaking the module's all-pointers-are-intp convention (sibling pointer-returning duckdb_vector_get_data at L236 correctly uses intp). This is real, not refuted: numba's IntegerModel/LLVM lower both intp (int64) and uint64 to the same i64 register width on every 64-bit ABI, so no data corruption occurs for realistic (always < 2^63) DuckDB counts/rows -- confirming the reviewer's own 'labeling, not corruption' characterization. Went further and found the vector_get_validity mismatch has a concrete (if minor) operational consequence beyond pure labeling: because @proxy dispatchers are eagerly compiled to a fixed signature, numba's typing does not silently unify a uint64 value with the intp argument type expected by duckdb_validity_row_is_valid's first parameter, so JIT call sites must add an explicit cast -- confirmed at test/test_ducklib.py:1118 ('intp(v3_validity_p)') and examples/irr.py:140-143 ('numpy.intp(ducklib.duckdb_vector_get_validity(vec_cf))', repeated x4 for cf/pd/inv/npv). This is stronger, concrete evidence for the defect than the original finding's speculative impact language ('could surprise numba callers'), but it still amounts to caller-side boilerplate/consistency friction rather than incorrect behavior, a crash, or silent data corruption, so 'low' severity is the right call -- not upgraded. All ducklib.py line citations (106, 156, 157, 226, 234, 237) checked directly against the current tree and match verbatim; the finding is accurately characterized and correctly scoped.
